answer:
RESULT — the data do NOT support a "Black advantage in BA completion" at any SES level; what they support is a steeper SES gradient for Black respondents, so the deficit is concentrated entirely at low SES and vanishes at/above median SES.

HYPOTHESIS (submission wording):
"Educational attainment rises much more steeply with family socioeconomic status for Black respondents than for non-Black non-Hispanic respondents in this NLSY79 cohort, so that the Black shortfall is confined to low-SES families and disappears at higher SES: below the pooled SES median, Black respondents completed grade 12 or more at 53.5% versus 74.1% for non-Black non-Hispanic respondents (gap −20.7 pp, 95% CI −27.0 to −14.4; RR 0.72), whereas at or above the median the two are statistically indistinguishable (89.2% vs 90.2%, gap −1.0 pp, 95% CI −6.3 to +4.2; RR 0.99), a race×SES interaction that is significant (Black-only LR χ² = 7.01, df 1, p = 0.008; interaction OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.19–4.06). The Black SES gradient is +35.7 pp (53.5 → 89.2) against +16.1 pp (74.1 → 90.2) for the comparison group: high family SES buys Black students roughly twice as much additional schooling but never lifts them above their socioeconomic peers — no SES stratum, including the descriptive grade≥16 appendix (Black 0.25% vs 0.38%, Fisher p = 0.52), shows a Black advantage — and because the extract measures education only in 1979 when respondents were 14–22 (only 37 respondents at grade ≥16 file-wide), true BA completion is unobserved and no BA-rate claim is supportable."

DESIGN AS EXECUTED
• Primary outcome P3 = grade≥12 at age≥20 in 1979 (n=3,487). Secondary: grade≥13 (n=12,532), ever-dorm enrolment proxy (n=11,601 observed). Appendix: grade≥16 descriptive.
• Granularity rule fired as pre-specified: tertiles FAILED (Black cells 257/108/86 — top cell n=86), so analysis used TWO levels at the pooled median. Final cells (primary): BLACK 303/148, HISP 479/239, ref 905/1,413; smallest 148 → no cell flagged n<50; tertile top cell flagged unreliable and kept descriptive only.
• SES = background-only z-mean of max(parental grade), occupation major-group prestige rank (validated against parental education and 1979 income: parental-ed z rises −0.88 → +1.39 from labourers 8xx to professional 0xx), log family income 1979; ≥2 of 3 items → 11,747/12,686 usable. Continuous −code version run as sensitivity.

EVIDENCE
1) Primary gap-by-SES table: below median BLACK 53.47% (n=303, Wilson 47.8–59.0) vs ref 74.14% (n=905) → −20.68 pp (−26.98, −14.38), RR 0.72 (0.64–0.81). At/above median BLACK 89.19% (n=148, 83.2–93.2) vs ref 90.23% (n=1,413) → −1.04 pp (−6.28, +4.19), RR 0.99 (0.93–1.05). Pooled: 65.19% vs 83.95%, −18.76 pp (−23.41, −14.12), RR 0.78. Hispanic −2.12 then −3.62 pp (both CIs cross 0).
2) Interaction LR tests: full 3-cohort χ²=9.329, df=2, p=0.0094; Black-only (n=2,769) χ²=7.014, df=1, p=0.0081. BLACK OR 0.403 (0.307–0.528) at low SES, interaction OR 2.199 (1.193–4.056), implied OR 0.886 at high SES; race main effect χ²=37.66, p=6.6e-09; SES OR 3.27; female OR 1.30. Model-predicted gaps (−20.4 / −1.1 pp) reproduce the raw table.
3) Tertile cross-check (shown as-is): gap −19.68 → −1.73 → −0.69 pp (RR 0.714 → 0.979 → 0.993).
4) Monotonicity verdict — my scoping glance was HALF REFUTED, as requested: "widest at low SES" CONFIRMED; "persists at high SES" REFUTED for background SES (gap ≈ −1 pp, CI includes 0). No stratum has RR > 1.05.
5) Secondary outcomes: grade≥13 — BLACK below ref at both levels (RR 0.74, 0.77), no SES variation (interaction χ²=1.11, df=2, p=0.573). Dorm enrolment proxy is non-monotone in the OPPOSITE direction (−0.53 pp / RR 0.88 below median; −8.73 pp / RR 0.44 at-above), reported unsmoothed; 91.4% coverage, coarse coding.
6) Robustness (gap_pp below / at-above median): primary −21.0/−0.2; continuous occupation −20.8/−1.2; complete-case −21.3/+1.6; occupation dropped −18.2/−3.0; parental education alone −21.5/−2.0; income-1979 alone −24.1/−13.0. Endogenous (post-outcome) measures: wealth85 −13.5/−12.4, wealth96 −20.2/−13.3, income85 −16.7/−12.9, income89 −20.3/−7.2, savings89 −19.0/−21.0 → direction (Black below reference) unchanged in every specification; the gap CLOSING at high SES holds only for 1979 background measures, as expected when conditioning on attainment's own consequences.
7) Missingness (no outcome imputation): index missing 8.3% Black / 12.6% Hispanic / 5.0% ref (occupation 34.3/47.5/22.4). Missing-indicator diagnostic: among the 273 primary-outcome respondents without a usable index the Black−ref gap is −16.7 pp (RR 0.73), same direction as the low-SES group, so index-missing respondents are not a high-SES reservoir inflating Black SES.
8) Appendix grade≥16 (descriptive): Black 5/1,975 (0.253%, exact CI 0.082–0.590), Hispanic 4/3,134, ref 28/7,423 (0.377%); by SES Black events 2 and 3; every Black cell <10 events, all Fisher p>0.5, all flagged. Every grade≥16 respondent was aged 19–22; 74.4% of Black respondents were <20 in 1979.
9) Ability control (attenuation, not mediation): ASVAB columns are mislabelled "Z Score" (raw mean ≈460, sd ≈90), standardised in-script; adding mean ASVAB Z on a common subsample (n=2,914) moves the BLACK OR at low SES from 0.423 to 1.105 and the interaction OR from 2.23 to 1.92 (ASVAB LR χ²=522.4).
10) Integrity: 12,686×61, unique IDs, 2 grade-95 sentinels → missing, top-coded money handled by rank-based cuts.

LIMITATIONS: observational, right-censored (education measured only in 1979, ages 14–22), unweighted, no wave/attrition flags; outcome is attainment not a degree; SES is a noisy 3-item background proxy with differential cohort missingness; reference group is non-Black non-Hispanic (Hispanic descriptive only); dorm proxy crude; the age≥20 restriction retains only the older ~30% of the cohort; ASVAB attenuation is not mediation. Association statement about SES-conditioned attainment gradients only.

payload.granularity_used: median_split (tertiles failed the pre-registered n>=100 cell rule: Black cells 257/108/86)
payload.hypothesis: Educational attainment rises far more steeply with family socioeconomic status for Black respondents than for non-Black non-Hispanic respondents in this NLSY79 cohort, so the Black attainment shortfall is concentrated entirely at low SES and disappears at higher SES: below the pooled SES median Black respondents completed grade 12 or more at 53.5% vs 74.1% for non-Black non-Hispanic respondents (gap -20.7 pp, 95% CI -27.0 to -14.4; RR 0.72), while at or above the median the groups are statistically indistinguishable (89.2% vs 90.2%; gap -1.0 pp, 95% CI -6.3 to +4.2; RR 0.99), a race-by-SES interaction confirmed by LR tests (Black-only chi2 = 7.01, df 1, p = 0.008; interaction OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.19-4.06). The Black SES gradient is +35.7 pp (53.5 to 89.2) versus +16.1 pp (74.1 to 90.2) for the comparison group, so high family background buys Black students about twice as much additional schooling but never lifts them above their socioeconomic peers - no SES stratum, including the descriptive grade>=16 appendix (Black 0.25% vs 0.38%, Fisher p = 0.52), shows a Black advantage - and true BA completion is unobserved in this extract (only 37 respondents at grade >= 16, 5 of them Black, measured when respondents were 14-22), so the finding is an association about SES-conditioned attainment gradients, not a causal or institutional claim.
payload.primary_outcome: highest grade completed 1979 >= 12 among respondents aged >= 20 (BA completion unobserved)
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61), cleaned sentinels (grade 95 -> missing, wealth -250 -> missing) and handled top-coded money variables via rank-based cuts. 2) Built outcome ladder: P3 primary = grade >= 12 among respondents aged >= 20 in 1979 (n=3,487); P1 = grade >= 13; P2 = ever DORM/FRATERNITY/SORORITY residence 1981-96; descriptive appendix = grade >= 16 with Wilson and exact CIs. 3) Built background SES index (z of max parental grade, z of occupation major-group prestige rank validated against parental education and 1979 income, z of log family income 1979; >= 2 of 3 items; 11,747 respondents). 4) Applied the pre-registered granularity rule: tertiles failed the n>=100 cell test (Black 257/108/86) so levels collapsed to below/at-or-above pooled median (smallest cell 148, none < 50); tertile results retained as flagged descriptive. 5) Stratified rate tables with Wilson CIs, percentage-point gaps and rate ratios (Black and Hispanic vs non-Black non-Hispanic reference). 6) Logistic models with age (linear+quadratic) and sex, BLACK x SES interaction and LR tests, plus model-predicted gaps. 7) Robustness: occupation prestige coding vs continuous -code, complete-case, occupation dropped, single-proxy indices, endogenous 1985-1996 wealth/income/savings direction checks, missing-indicator diagnostic; no outcome imputation. 8) ASVAB mean-Z attenuation check on a common subsample (reported as attenuation, not mediation). 9) Wrote tables, model summaries and RESULTS_summary.md under outputs/.
